title: Drift confined to lore:tasks managed blocks is a warning by default and an error only under --strict
description: DEC-282 item 3, filed from ODOC-610 (opum-doc, 2026-11-18T23:03Z). VERBATIM: 'lore-cli: drift confined to lore:tasks blocks is a warning by default, and an error with --strict. Every other managed-block drift stays an error. quest does not rewrite lore blocks.' CONTEXT from the report: any quest write staled the lore:tasks rollup, so lore check exited 6 and everyone re-ran sync and check defensively. That defensive re-running is part of what turned a stale rollup into a process storm. Ships in the next lore/quest pair (DEC-282 items 1-4 ship together).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Drift confined to lore:tasks managed blocks is a warning by default, with the exit code recorded.
--strict turns that same drift into an error, with the exit code recorded.
Every other managed-block drift (any non-lore:tasks block) stays an error in both modes.
tests cover both ways for both modes: lore:tasks drift warns by default and errors under --strict; another block drift errors in both.
quest does not rewrite lore blocks: the boundary is stated and pinned by a test or a documented invariant.

DISPOSITION: CI then caught docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh:962 (a row asserting exit 6 for block-body drift, red on the required docker e2e check); fixed in 64ddd5ae (expect 0 by default plus a new --strict step expecting 6), which the reviewer did not see and a Sonnet unit reviews. VERDICT: APPROVE 50c41561 (two non-blocking doc nits)
Confinement is implemented correctly, and I found no way to downgrade other drift. I read the code only and could not run anything.
How the confinement is decided. There is no explicit "confined to lore:tasks" predicate. The only code change is `severity: "error"` to `"warning"` on the `managed-block-drift` push at src/core/check.ts:907-913. The exit code comes from the existing `exitFor` (src/commands/check.ts:967-977), which fails on `errorCount - indeterminate > 0 || (strict && warningCount > 0)`. So "confined" means "no error-tier finding exists", and that is exactly what you want. `managed-block-drift` is emitted only from that one site, and `regenerateTaskBlock` rewrites only the `lore:tasks` region. `index-drift` and `schema-drift` are separate rules, untouched and still error. `status-drift` is still error at src/core/check.ts:894. A corrupted, duplicated or missing marker still throws from `regenerateTaskBlock`, which is called at src/core/check.ts:900 before the push. The catch at src/commands/check.ts:1204-1208 keeps the error and the run rejects, so it can never become the soft warning.
Your five questions: 1. Confinement: sound, as above. Drift in other managed blocks or outside the markers has no path into this finding. 2. Mixed report: any error gives `errorCount > 0`, so exit 6 without `--strict`. The new tests cover status-drift + block drift (test/check.test.ts:2393-2410) and index-drift + block drift (test/check.test.ts:3281-3309), each in both modes. 3. `--strict`: unchanged. It escalates every warning, as it always did. The only finding that moved tiers is this one, so it is now escalated. Test at test/check.test.ts:2379-2391. 4. Changed tests: legitimate. The two flipped to `EXIT_OK` (test/check.test.ts ~2975 and ~3004) have status matching, so they are pure block drift. They gained severity and rule assertions, so they are stronger, not weaker. The tests that still expect 6 — 2430 (uses `--strict`), 2798 and 2866 (a frontmatter error sits beside the drift) — remain valid. Other tests expecting 6 are unaffected: 2448 (mixed), 2460 (status drift) and 2830/2839 (thrown). 5. Docs, ADR amendment, CHANGELOG and docstrings are accurate and consistent with the code.
Findings: LOW (docs, stale): docs/reference/cli-contract.md:470-472 says `drift` "can tell … 'my managed block is stale'" at exit 6. A bare stale `lore:tasks` block no longer exits 6 by default, so that example is now misleading. LOW (docs, stale): docs/reference/architecture.md:297-300 says "stale managed blocks … Exit `6` on drift". It should say that a bare `lore:tasks` block is a warning by default. INFO: The repo's own `lore check (docs gate)` CI job, and any caller that treats exit 0 as "no task drift", now passes with a stale `lore:tasks` block unless it passes `--strict`. This is the intended DEC-282 behaviour, and the CHANGELOG says so. You may want to confirm whether this repo's own gate should adopt `--strict`. I saw no scripts/ or docker/ reference to the old behaviour. INFO: A multi-root run where one root's block drift would otherwise be the only finding behaves the same way (exit 0, warning). Covered by the changed multi-root test.
Could not verify without a shell: that the tests pass, and the red/green and mutation evidence the writer claims; a text-mode (non-JSON) run, to see that the warning renders in the warn stream with its hint; every `lore check` call site in `.github/` and `docker/` (I grepped for managed-block terms only, not for each invocation's reliance on exit 6); the long line at docs/reference/cli-surface.md:433, which came back truncated in my grep.

Scope: I read the delta 50c41561..64ddd5ae (docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh, +5 -1) and the full PR diff. I also read run-e2e.sh:860-1030, 1350-1440 and 1505-1525, plus docker/e2e/lib/steps.sh:60-210 for the step, step_json, step_fail and check helpers. The rest of what I read is in the sweep and doc sections below. Every result here comes from reading the files. I ran nothing.

(a) The contract is stated correctly: by default `lore check` exits 0 on `lore:tasks` block-body drift, and under `--strict` it exits 6. The delta changes no other assertion's text. But it fails both "musts" in the brief: one step can pass without testing anything, and one assertion it left unchanged no longer proves what it did.

F1 — BLOCKING — docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh:964-965. The default step can pass without testing anything.
- The `sed` at :961 ends in `|| true`, so if it matches nothing, nothing notices. Phase 6b (:870) has a `check` that confirms its seed took. This seed has none.
- `step … 0 -- lore check` exits 0 whether the block is drifted or not. The old `6` was what proved the fixture had drifted.
- The `--strict` step at :966 only covers this if the bundle carries no other warning at that point. `--strict` promotes every deterministic warning, so any unrelated warning would also produce the 6. Nothing before :961 shows the bundle is warning-free; :954 checks only for exit 0, and a warning still exits 0.
- Fix: replace :964-965 with a `step_json`. `step_json` already requires exit 0, so one assertion proves the fixture drifted and pins the new default severity:
  `step_json "lore check: managed-block BODY drift is a warning by default (exit 0, finding present)" '.data.errorCount == 0 and any(.data.findings[]; .rule == "managed-block-drift" and .severity == "warning")' -- lore check --json`
- Don't pin `.file` to `$STORY_PATH`. Findings use bundle-relative paths (`stories/x.md` in the unit tests), and the harness variable is probably repo-relative, so an exact match could fail for the wrong reason.

F2 — BLOCKING — docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh:969. This line is unchanged, but its assertion is now weaker.
- `step "lore check: clean again after healing the block-body drift" 0 -- lore check` used to prove that `lore sync "$STORY_ID"` at :968 actually healed the block, because unhealed drift exited 6. Now unhealed drift also exits 0, so the step proves nothing.
- Phase 17a (:1520, `warningCount == 0`) does not back this up. The full `lore sync --json` at :1424 would re-heal the block before Phase 17a runs, so a :968 that didn't heal would never show up.
- Fix: `step_json "lore check: clean again after healing the block-body drift" '[.data.findings[] | select(.rule == "managed-block-drift")] | length == 0' -- lore check --json`.
- Optional, stronger: `step "…" 0 -- lore check --strict`. That would also show the 6 at :966 came from the drift. Use it only after checking that the bundle is warning-free at that point; nobody has measured that.

===== <teammate-message teammate_id="lore-cli-review-744r2" color="yellow" summary="PR744 round-2 delta verdict: APPROVE">
VERDICT: APPROVE at 4c08da67b587031da96c23e94b327250976f4a98

Reviewer unit (read-only, DEC-183) for the round-2 delta on opum-ai/lore-cli#744 (LCLI-793), 64ddd5ae..4c08da67. I read the code only and ran nothing.

(d) Scope: the delta is exactly one file, docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh, +6/-3. It turns two `step` calls into `step_json` calls, at :964-966 and :970-972, and changes one step name. Nothing else changed. The two old step names are not pinned anywhere else in the repo (I grepped test/, docker/ and src/). The number of cases is the same, because each step became one step_json, so the assert_non_vacuous floor still holds.

(a) Prior F1 is closed exactly as asked, with `.file` left unpinned. `.data.errorCount == 0 and any(.data.findings[]; .rule == "managed-block-drift" and .severity == "warning")` on `lore check --json`:
- If the `sed ... || true` at :961 matches nothing, the block does not drift, no managed-block-drift finding is produced, `any` is false, and the step fails. The seed is now asserted rather than assumed.
- If the seed also reaches the frontmatter, status-drift is an error, so errorCount is at least 1 and the exit is 6. The step fails on both conjuncts.

Prior F2 is closed exactly as asked: `[.data.findings[] | select(.rule == "managed-block-drift")] | length == 0`, with no `--strict`. If `lore sync "$STORY_ID"` does not heal the block, the warning stays. The exit is still 0 by default, but length is 1 or more, so the filter returns false and the step fails. It is also not vacuous on a missing field: `.data.findings` being null makes jq error with "Cannot iterate over null", and empty stdout makes `jq -e` produce no result. Both are non-zero, so both fail. F1 at :964 has just proved that drift detection runs on this bundle, which is the positive control for F2's empty result.

(b) Rule id and severity: src/core/check.ts:907-912 emits `{severity: "warning", rule: "managed-block-drift"}` for lore:tasks body drift, which is the regenerateTaskBlock mismatch. Status drift has its own distinct id, `{severity: "error", rule: "status-drift"}` at check.ts:893-898, so it cannot match by accident. Its error severity would fail F1's errorCount conjunct anyway. The envelope shape is `{kind: "check.report", data: CheckReport}` (src/commands/check.ts:1650-1653), and CheckReport carries `findings`, `errorCount` and `warningCount` (check.ts:985-989). exitFor (check.ts:967-977) returns 0 when there are warnings only and strict is off, so step_json's exit-0 conjunct agrees with the new default.

(c) Quoting: both filters are single-quoted at the call site, so the shell expands nothing in `$`, `[`, `|` or `"`. step_json (docker/e2e/lib/steps.sh:91-112) passes the filter as `jq -e "$filter" "$out"`, a quoted expansion, so it arrives intact as one argument. It requires `rc -eq 0 && jq -e ...`. `jq -e` exits 1 when the last output is false or null, so a jq `false` is a FAIL. stdout and stderr go to separate files, so stderr advisories cannot corrupt the JSON.

F1 (NIT, outside this delta: the lines came in at 64ddd5ae and have not changed since): docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh:967-968. `step "lore check --strict: ..." 6` is still a bare exit-code check. Under `--strict`, any warning already in the bundle gives exit 6. :954 only proves errorCount==0, not that there are no warnings, so this step does not prove that THIS drift is what gates. The previous review's "not warning-free unless measured" caveat implies the same thing. The F1 step before it now establishes that the drift exists, so this is not a blocking gap. Optional fix: capture the output and use `check` to assert rc == 6 and `jq -e '.data.errorCount == 0 and any(.data.findings[]; .rule == "managed-block-drift")'`. step_fail does not fit here, because --strict still writes the report to stdout. Alternatively, add a `step_json '.data.warningCount == 0'` before :961 to measure the bundle as warning-free. Neither is required for merge.
